Assertions.Description: Clean-profile Settings/OOBE calls the module Shortcut Guide and describes the app-aware overlay, not V2.
Disabled from first render, with no transient Shortcut Guide process/event activation.
Enabling persists across a PowerToys restart.
A fresh guide closes once with Escape, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once with the configured chord, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once with its title-bar Close button, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once when clicking the transparent area outside the pane, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once when another tracked app becomes foreground, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
The configured physical chord opens the non-elevated guide above an elevated Notepad fixture.
A safe displayed Windows shortcut such as Win+E opens the expected Explorer fixture and closes the guide; close only that Explorer fixture.
With notepad.exe excluded and the fixture foreground, the configured chord opens no guide surface.
With notepad.exe excluded and the fixture foreground, the configured Windows-key action opens no guide surface.
With the exclusion still present, foreground Explorer and confirm the guide opens.
Remove the exclusion and confirm Notepad activation works without restarting Windows.
After warm-up, ten open/navigate/close cycles reuse the same PID with functional navigation/content and at most one visible overlay in each cycle.
Private working set after the ten cycles and two-second idle increases by no more than 32 MiB from the warm baseline.
Desktop activation succeeds without a blank-title fault.
Windows and PowerToys vector rail entries are readable and one is selected.
Selected page has Pinned, Recommended where applicable, normal headings and shortcut key caps.
The rail Settings icon is fully visible; invoking it opens the existing Settings window directly to Shortcut Guide.
Pin from a row context menu creates one Pinned row and records it for the correct application in Pinned.json.
The row remains pinned after dismissing and reopening the guide.
Unpin removes the row immediately and restores localized empty-state text; restore the original Pinned.json.
After backing up and removing the per-user shortcuts directory, guide invocation recreates the directory and index.
Every bundled manifest in the tested build is copied and referenced exactly once; every copied YAML parses.
Windows, PowerToys, Explorer and Notepad pages remain available without a launch crash; restore the original directory.
A disposable Notepad-filtered manifest renders virtual-key 65, <1>, <LessThan>, <GreaterThan> and an arrow as A, 1, <, > and the expected arrow glyph/name, not raw numbers/tokens.
Empty and unknown keys in that manifest neither crash the guide nor suppress valid sibling shortcuts.
After changing to a supported non-English PowerToys language and restarting, Shortcut Guide Settings labels are localized without resource keys or unintended English fallback.
Title, search, Close, Settings, Pinned, Recommended, Taskbar, Pin/Unpin and no-results text are localized; application-manifest names/descriptions may remain English. Restore the original language.

With different DPI scales on two monitors, foreground Notepad on each in turn: full guide appears on that foreground monitor, stays within its work area and has no double scaling, gap, spill or cross-monitor offset.
On each differently scaled monitor in turn, taskbar-indicator mode appears on the foreground monitor within its work area and aligns to its taskbar without double scaling, gap, spill or offset.
